newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Golds help Australian stocks shine at open.
newsitem.headline: Golds help Australian stocks shine at open.

text.p: Firmer base metals prices and a shining performance from the gold sector after a bounce in the bullion price boosted Australian stocks at the open on Friday.
The All Ordinaries index climbed 14.8 points to 2,684.5.
Predictably, the miners made most of the gains, with key majors higher and the gold sector index posting gains of over three percent early.
"It's a very encouraging sign although most people are still treating it with a bit of caution," said Hartley Poynton broker, Dirk Van der Struyf, noting the strong performance from golds.

Among the golds, Acacia Resources added 3.7 percent to A$1.39 (A$1.02), sector heavyweight Normandy Mining jumped 2.6 percent to A$1.57, while Newcrest Mining climbed three percent to A$2.78. Rumoured takeover target of Barrick Gold Corp, Great Central Mines NL, was 1.9 percent up at A$2.69.
In the leaders, BHP was up 14 cents to A$18.60, while Rio Tinto was 18 cents higher at A$21.74.
"The weakness in the Australian dollar has helped some of these bigger players," Van der Struyf said.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to three, while about 33 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
